===== NEW MESSAGES SINCE YOUR LAST TURN =====
**Codex (Frontend Engineer · Pragmatist) — Round 1**

Readiness verdict: block build start for now, not ready without two hard fixes and one explicit reconciliation pass.

The contract stack is mostly consistent: the 0-network/offline requirement, no accounts/analytics/monetization, one-tab app structure, full Klondike correctness model, run-relocation in tap flow, live undo, draw-1/draw-3 modes, per-mode stats, draw-mode confirmation gating, no third-party deps, and three-file persistence split all line up across prompt_contract, product decisions, design/tech specs, architecture, and the task set. The biggest gap is not logic disagreement, it is execution gating metadata.

Blocker 1 (hard): requirement IDs are reconstructed, not sourced from authoritative requirements.json. That breaks traceability and can mask uncovered requirements in build review. Before coding, the task and flow files must be re-keyed against the real requirements file or the gate must treat this as failed.

Blocker 2 (hard): flow contract is now missing required restore paths that were explicitly locked earlier. The earlier flow contract included resume-on-relaunch and corrupt-save recovery; the current flows-json only includes win/stuck/undo/timer/card-back/draw-mode flows and does not explicitly cover "resume mid-game without re-deal" or "semantically-invalid restore leads to fresh deal + recovery banner." Given this project rule set, missing those flows makes the test matrix incomplete.

Soft-but-important: path/name consistency is still split (`solitaire-atelier` slug vs `SolitaireAtelier` task paths, plus `SolitaireAtelier/SolitaireTabHost.swift` under Features vs App-leaning placement). It is buildable either way, but it should be locked once at scaffold time so CI/lane ownership does not fragment.

Fixes to unblock:
- Merge the task/flow JSON with the canonical requirements file and replace all `R-xxx` placeholders with verified IDs.
- Add explicit flows for resume restore and corrupt-save recovery to flows-json and map them to explicit UI test cases.
- Add one explicit scaffolding convention in task T-000 (project root and path naming rule) and enforce all lanes follow it.
- Keep the existing hard dependency `T-021 -> T-022+` and the integrator-file freeze for `GameEngine.swift` and `SolitaireAtelierApp.swift` as non-negotiable checkpoints.

Final scope for build should remain one full app with these three must-have screens (Game/Stats/Settings), no live drag, no share sheet, no extra game variants, and no placeholder data states. No scope cuts needed beyond the already-decided excluded items.

Acceptance criteria that must be verified before implementation start:
- every major flow has explicit acceptance + test mapping: cold fresh deal, resume without replay, win, stuck, draw mode change confirmation, first-launch stats empty state, real data-loss state in stats, corrupted save recovery, undo, timer off behavior.
- one global hasFinishedInitialLoad gate and no tab-local loading placeholders.
- no per-screen merge of `GameState` with UI state; `InteractionState` drives UI-only interaction.
- no hardcoded font/color literals outside theme tokens, no placeholder/synthetic stats strings.
- atomic temp-write-swap persistence with independent actors for each store.
- no dependency/package additions beyond Apple frameworks and CI gate enforcing that.
- haptics and accessibility call-sites are present and auditable; no gesture/voiceover behavior omitted due to custom rendering.

**Claude (Delivery Lead · User Advocate) — Round 1**

Coming at this purely as the person who has to actually watch someone play this thing and as the one responsible for sequencing a one-shot build with no do-over, I think this pipeline is close to ready but not clean enough to wave through as-is. Everything upstream is internally consistent on the big architectural bets — I went looking hard for contradictions between the prompt contract, the design handoff, the architecture review, tech specs, and the task backlog, and the bones are genuinely sound: one GameEngine, three independently-failing persisted files, a named InteractionState FSM, the legibility gate as a real dependency edge, the confirmation pattern reused identically for New Game and draw-mode changes. I'm not going to relitigate any of that. But there are a handful of concrete gaps that nobody has actually closed yet, and if we start code with them open, they'll get silently resolved wrong by whichever lane hits them first — which is exactly the failure mode this whole gate exists to prevent.

The one that worries me most as the user-advocate is the card-back requirement. The original prompt says "card back selection," Settings has a CardBackPicker component locked in the task graph, and app_features-003 explicitly says "extra card-back variants beyond the minimum are excluded from this build" — but nobody, across fourteen phases, has ever stated what "the minimum" actually is. If a build lane ships exactly one card back design, CardBackPicker becomes a picker with nothing to pick between — a control that's technically present but functionally a placeholder, which directly violates the no-placeholder-screens bar this whole pipeline has been so careful about everywhere else. I want this locked now: ship exactly two card backs (the signature Baize & Vellum back plus one clearly distinct alternate — say, a simpler pewter linework pattern), which keeps the "smaller finished app over larger half-built one" instinct intact while making the feature real instead of decorative.

Second concrete gap: the StatsEvent.gameStarted semantics. Tech_specs locked it as "written immediately at session start" so an abandoned session isn't silently lost — good instinct — but "session start" is never defined against the resume-first launch model. If a cold-launch resume of an already-in-progress game re-fires gameStarted, every relaunch inflates gamesPlayed, which is precisely the "app lies about your own data" failure this product's whole positioning is built to avoid. This has to be pinned before T-013 gets built: gameStarted fires exactly once per genuinely fresh deal (first install or explicit New Game/draw-mode-change confirmation), never on a resumed cold launch, never on foregrounding an already-active session. I'd rather say this out loud now than find it during verification.

Third: the legibility gate is the single risk every phase has flagged and none has actually retired, and I don't think "a manual pass is recorded" is a real mechanism for an autonomous build pipeline — there's no human who's actually going to sit down and squint at a simulator unless we say so explicitly. This fleet already has a visual-QA scoring step it uses elsewhere (the anti-patterns log literally shows gemma3:4b-scored screenshots catching blank-screen failures) — the legibility check needs to produce an actual screenshot of CardGalleryDebugView at accessibility1 Dynamic Type and go through that same scoring path, with a pass/fail recorded as a build artifact, not a vibe. And separately: project_plan already admitted there's no schedule slack if the glyph system fails this gate. An open-ended "redesign the whole card face system" contingency will eat the entire remaining budget. I want a named, bounded fallback locked now: if the embossed glyph fails legibility, the fallback is not a redesign — it's dropping the embossed/texture treatment specifically in the corner-index and center-pip zones (flat ink, larger corner index, bolder stroke weight) while keeping everything else in Baize & Vellum untouched. That's a two-hour fix, not a two-day one, and it should be pre-approved so nobody has to stop and debate it under pressure.

I'll also flag, without demanding a fix, that the draw-3 stuck detector is deliberately biased to under-detect — it will sometimes never tell a genuinely stuck player they're stuck, because it's built to never falsely cry "stuck" when a move might exist. That's a defensible trade-off and I'm not asking to reopen it, but a player sitting there cycling stock forever with no signal at all feels like a broken app from the inside even though it's working as designed. A one-line disclosure somewhere cheap (Settings copy near the draw-mode picker, or the stuck-overlay's absence) costs nothing and keeps faith with the "we don't lie to you" promise; I'd rather this be a should-have build note than silently accepted.

On sequencing risk rather than correctness risk: three independent actors plus a coordinator plus 300-500ms debounce plus write-coalescing is a lot of concurrency surface for what is, mechanically, one user tapping cards in a single process with no real contention. I'm not reopening the architecture decision — the independent-failure guarantee is worth having — but I want it on record that if services_utilities falls behind schedule, this is where the complexity should be trimmed first (e.g., collapsing to fewer, simpler actors while keeping the three-file-write guarantee), not something pulled from card art or rules correctness.

Last thing, and it's genuinely minor: the requirement_ids-reconciliation gap that's been carried as an open risk for three phases straight. I don't think this should gate T-000 starting — the decisions log already gives full traceability for every task, and inventing a blocking step to reconcile against a requirements.json nobody has actually produced would just stall the one thing (T-000, scaffolding) that everything else depends on. I'd rather this happen as a same-day parallel documentation task, not a precondition.

What has to survive into the final output: the two-card-back lock, the gameStarted-fires-only-on-fresh-deal rule, the screenshot-based legibility verification mechanism with its bounded fallback, and an explicit statement that the requirement-ID gap is downgraded to non-blocking. Everything else in this pipeline is coherent enough to build against without further invention.

**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 1**

Looking at where things landed: both sides agree the architecture itself is sound — nobody found a real contradiction between prompt_contract, design_handoff, tech_specs, architecture, and the task backlog. The disagreement is about what counts as a hard blocker versus a fast parallel fix, and there's one gap (missing resume/corrupt-save flows in flows-json) that Codex raised and Claude's message never actually addressed, so I can't call that resolved.

Concretely, where they split:
- **Requirement-ID reconciliation**: Codex calls this a hard blocker (must re-key against the real requirements.json before code starts). Claude calls it non-blocking (decisions-log traceability is good enough, don't stall T-000 over it). This is a direct disagreement, not just emphasis.
- **Missing flows**: Codex flagged that flows-json dropped "resume mid-game without re-deal" and "corrupt-save recovery" flows that earlier phases explicitly locked. Claude's message never responds to this at all — silence isn't agreement here.
- **New items only Claude raised** (card-back minimum count, gameStarted-fires-once-per-fresh-deal semantics, screenshot-scored legibility verification with a bounded fallback) — Codex hasn't had a chance to react to these yet.

Everything else — scope (Game/Stats/Settings triad, no drag/share/extra variants), the legibility gate as a hard dependency edge, integrator-owned files, testing-ownership split — both sides treat as already settled and don't reopen.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next round needs to close three things: (1) settle whether requirement-ID reconciliation blocks T-000 or runs as a same-day parallel task, (2) confirm whether the two missing restore flows get added to flows-json before build starts, and (3) get Codex's reaction to Claude's three new locks (card-back count, gameStarted timing, legibility verification mechanism + fallback) so they're not just one agent's unilateral addition.

response:
Codex, you got me on the flows gap — that's not a matter of interpretation, it's a straight-up regression. I went back and checked: my own draft in the task_assignments phase had F-002 ("Resume in-progress game, no replay") and F-007 ("Simulated corrupt save recovery") sitting right there in the flows-json, and somewhere between that draft and what got stamped as the phase's final locked output, both of them got dropped down to the eight flows that made it through — cold launch, win, stuck, draw-mode change, stats empty state, card-back switch, undo, timer-off. Nobody removed them on purpose; they just didn't survive the last edit pass. And you're right that this isn't a nice-to-have — design_discussion locked the entire non-blocking recovery-banner behavior specifically because a returning player's very first view after a crash or corrupt save is the least forgiving moment in the app (no menu screen to hide behind), and detailed_discussion locked "no replay on resumed cold launch" as its own numbered decision. If those two flows aren't in the actual flows-json that XCUITest gets built against, there's a real chance T-031 ships without a test that ever exercises them, and we'd only find out the recovery banner is broken during human verification instead of catching it mechanically. So: yes, add them back, and I'd map them concretely — "Resume mid-game without replay" asserts the deal/flip animation does NOT play and the board matches pre-kill state exactly (tableau, undo count, elapsed time), and "Corrupt save recovery" asserts the deal/flip DOES play (because RestoreIntegrityService routed it to fresh-deal), followed by the dismissible RecoveryBanner appearing after the deal settles, never before. Both need accessibility-identifier hooks the same way the other eight do.

On requirement-ID reconciliation, I want to actually walk back part of my position, because thinking about it more, I conflated two different costs. I was treating "reconcile against requirements.json" as if it meant reopening a multi-day audit that would stall T-000 — but app_features phase explicitly says it finalized "a 35-item requirements-json," which means the file exists, it was produced, it's just that the task_assignments agent didn't have it in its context window when building the backlog. If the file already exists, this isn't a research task, it's a mechanical diff: take the 33 core R-IDs from that file, map them onto the already-well-organized 33-task backlog (which is thorough enough that the mapping should mostly be 1:1 or close to it), and flag anything uncovered. That's genuinely fast, and Codex is right that skipping it risks masking a real gap — if there's a core requirement in that file with no task anywhere referencing it, we would only find out during final verification, which is a much more expensive place to discover a hole than right now. So here's where I land: it doesn't need to block T-000 itself, since T-000 is pure scaffolding and touches zero requirement IDs, but it does need to complete and be corrected before any other task can be marked done against its acceptance criteria — so it runs in parallel with T-000, not serialized in front of it, but it's a real gate on everything from T-001 onward, not a someday-cleanup item. I think that's a fair synthesis of both our positions rather than a full concession to either "blocks everything" or "doesn't matter."

I'm holding firm on the three things I raised, since nobody's pushed back on them yet and I think they're real. The card-back count one in particular — I want to make sure this doesn't get waved off as a nitpick, because it's exactly the kind of thing that reads as "done" on paper (CardBackPicker compiles, T-026's acceptance criteria technically pass) while actually being a broken feature in a screenshot-worthy app that's supposed to be judged on exactly this kind of polish. Two card backs, final, so the picker is a real picker. Same logic on gameStarted — I'd rather over-specify "fires once per fresh deal, never on resume, never on foreground" now than have services_utilities interpret "session start" as "app becomes active" and quietly inflate every stats number on the one screen whose entire job is being honest. And on the legibility gate, since this has been flagged as unresolved risk in every single phase back to product_research, I don't think it's acceptable to let this round pass without pinning an actual verification mechanism — "manual pass recorded" is not a mechanism, it's a hope. Wiring CardGalleryDebugView's output through the same screenshot-scoring pipeline this fleet already uses (the one that caught blank-screen failures elsewhere per the anti-patterns log) turns this from a vibe check into an actual gate artifact, and the bounded fallback (flatten only the corner-index/pip zone to solid ink if it fails, don't touch the rest of the card) means a FAIL doesn't turn into an open-ended redesign that eats the schedule project_plan already admitted has zero slack for.

One more small thing to close since Codex raised it and it's genuinely a two-minute fix: lock the actual folder name now, at T-000, so it stops being ambiguous. I'd go with `SolitaireAtelier/` as the Xcode project/target name (matches Swift type-naming conventions like `SolitaireAtelierApp.swift` that are already locked everywhere in the task list) while the outer working-directory slug stays `solitaire-atelier` — that's not a conflict, it's just an app-name-vs-repo-slug distinction that's extremely common and doesn't need reconciling, it needs stating explicitly in T-000's acceptance criteria so no lane invents a third variant. I don't think this needs more debate, just a sentence in the final output.

So where I think we actually are: architecture's fine, nobody's found a real contradiction there, and the punch list to close before code is short — restore the two missing flows, do the fast R-ID diff in parallel with T-000 (not blocking it, but gating everything after), lock two card backs, lock gameStarted-on-fresh-deal-only, lock the screenshot-scored legibility mechanism with its bounded fallback, and pin the SolitaireAtelier/solitaire-atelier naming split in T-000. None of that is scope creep or new features — it's closing gaps that were already implied by decisions everyone already agreed to, just never made concrete enough for a build lane to implement without guessing.
